name: EngiCore
short: A unified workspace for the engineering tasks that cannot afford fragmented workflows.
lead: EngiCore brings project file operations, document utilities and repeatable engineering tasks into one familiar Windows environment.
problem: Engineering teams frequently switch among folders, spreadsheets and small utilities to manage the same project information. That fragmentation makes simple tasks hard to repeat consistently.
features: Job-oriented file management and structured project utilities
DWG, PDF, material-code and barcode related workflows
Reporting, naming and document-organization helpers
Practical Windows interface for repeatable everyday tasks
results: Fewer context switches between day-to-day engineering utilities
Repeatable processes instead of manual folder operations
Project-focused workflows built for real users

name: Checker’s Tool
short: One checking workspace for spool drawings, JDE references and project-specific rules.
lead: A multi-job engineering checking application designed around spool visibility, source-data lookups, drawing retrieval and controlled checks.
problem: Drawing checkers must reconcile spool numbers, source systems, ISO references, revisions and job-specific requirements while keeping their work traceable.
features: Separate job modules with project-specific mappings and references
Spool, line, PDF, JDE and drawing lookup workflows
Checking status, priority, aging and spool monitoring
Administrative controls for job settings, notices and users
results: Faster retrieval of related spool information
More consistent checking workflows across projects
Better visibility into outstanding engineering checks

name: Spool Support Sync
short: Match the right spool with the right support information without repetitive PDF work.
lead: A dedicated support coordination utility that aligns Excel support references with spool drawing packages and automates document assembly.
problem: Spool and support documents may live in different locations. Manual attachment assembly can be slow and leaves room for omission.
features: Spool identification and matching against support references
Excel-driven support reference management
Single-spool and batch PDF attachments and merging
Processing feedback, logs and user-friendly controls
results: Traceable matching of spool and support information
Consistent output for engineering release packages

name: DWG Batch Editor
short: Structured drawing updates, executed across batches rather than one file at a time.
lead: An AutoCAD-oriented Windows utility for repeated drawing metadata changes across large sets of fabrication deliverables.
problem: Changing title blocks, identifiers, revisions and associated data manually on many drawings takes time and increases inconsistent output.
features: Read structured metadata and mappings from Excel
Batch replacement of drawing and spool identifiers
Revision, barcode, project and title-block data handling
DWG/PDF generation flows with execution logs

name: Multiple Spool Merger
short: Turn scattered spool PDFs and suffix drawings into ordered, traceable packages.
lead: An automated merger that recognizes spool identifiers, groups related drawing PDFs and processes document packages at scale.
problem: Spool drawings frequently arrive as a base PDF plus lettered attachments. Manually combining them and identifying missing sheets is repetitive.
features: Group PDFs by spool number and drawing suffix
Merge corresponding base and attachment pages in sequence
Batch folder processing with progress and exception feedback
Missing-attachment handling and output naming conventions
results: Less time spent collating PDF attachments

name: Support DPR
short: A structured daily progress workflow for assignments, checks and release reporting.
lead: A daily progress reporting application focused on fabrication-support work, role-based handovers and transparent team activity.
problem: Daily engineering progress can be fragmented between individual trackers, handover messages and manually consolidated reports.
features: Assignment and progress tracking across checking stages
User and role-oriented work views
Daily, weekly and monthly reporting outputs
Configurable reporting sources and audit-friendly records

name: Ship-Loose BOM & PDF Generator
short: Generate coordinated ship-loose drawings and BOM workbooks from one structured input.
lead: A template-driven ship-loose document generator being refined against real fabrication references.
problem: Ship-loose sheets demand consistent identifiers, barcodes, title blocks, piecemarks and well-aligned tables. Rebuilding them manually invites formatting differences.
features: Paired drawing PDF and BOM workbook output
Matching naming for drawing-to-BOM traceability
Barcode, piecemark and drawing metadata layout
Configurable project/customer settings and precise table alignment
results: One-to-one naming between drawing and BOM

name: Spool Drawing Maker
short: A visual tool concept for creating fabrication-oriented spool drawings from engineering inputs.
lead: An evolving engineering application focused on practical spool geometry, isometric conventions and fabrication-ready drawing output.
problem: Preparing fabrication-style piping drawings requires accurate dimensions, component placement, correct elbow geometry and readable technical presentation.
features: Spool layouts built from piping components and dimensions
Metric and imperial dimension handling
Fabrication drawing previews and document generation
Exploration of PCF and standard piping-component references

name: Engineering Workflow Automations
short: Targeted utilities for BOMs, joint data, job cards, SharePoint and reporting.
lead: A growing collection of practical automations to remove repetitive steps across engineering data and document processes.
problem: Engineering workflows often depend on extracts that must be compared, cleaned, merged, checked and distributed accurately.
features: BOM and joint-data reconciliation with backups and change logs
Job-card extraction and Power Query transformations
Excel / VBA reporting and structured data preparation
Power Automate, SharePoint and source-system integrations
results: Less manual reconciliation and copy-paste work
